prompt: Show that the rate of change of momentum Delta p / Delta t simplifies to ma for a body of constant mass m.

mark_scheme.criterion: Writes Delta p / Delta t = Delta(mv) / Delta t = m(Delta v / Delta t).
Substitutes a = Delta v / Delta t to obtain ma and explicitly states that mass m must be constant.

hints: Express change in momentum Delta p as m(v - u) when mass is constant.
Recall that acceleration is defined as rate of change of velocity (Delta v / Delta t).
solution: Delta p / Delta t = Delta(mv) / Delta t. When mass m is constant, this becomes m(Delta v / Delta t). Because acceleration a = Delta v / Delta t, the expression simplifies to ma.
teacher_walkthrough: Start with the definition F = Delta p / Delta t.
Factor out mass m under the condition that mass is constant: m * (Delta v / Delta t).
Substitute a = Delta v / Delta t to complete the proof: F = ma.
